passage: At the Rotterdam warehouse, Lucia was closing the last delivery when Mateo pulled her by the shelves. "I skipped the crane check this morning, no time. I signed the sheet anyway. Keep it quiet, yes? You'd do it for me." She liked Mateo. He had covered her shift when her mother was ill. Her stomach tightened. "Mateo, I can't lie for you. If someone asks me, I'll tell the truth." He blinked. "So what do I do?" "Do the check now, before the afternoon shift, and tell the supervisor it was late. I'll stay with you while you do it." They walked to the crane together in silence. Lucia was not sure Mateo forgave her, but she felt lighter than if she had joined the silence.

qa.q: Why did Lucia's stomach tighten when Mateo asked her to keep quiet?
qa.a: Lucia felt torn: she liked Mateo and owed him for covering her shift, but she could not lie for him.

qa.q: What could Lucia do if Mateo refuses to tell the supervisor?
qa.a: She can remind Mateo she will not lie if asked, encourage him again, and report it to the supervisor herself if the risk continues.

qa.q: How might Mateo have felt when Lucia refused?
qa.a: He blinked and asked what to do, so he was probably surprised and worried. He may also have felt let down by a friend, since Lucia was not sure he forgave her.

grounding: A friendly colleague asks the protagonist to keep quiet about his shortcut; she urges him to fix it and says she cannot lie for him.
